immortalize

ih-MOR-tuh-lyze · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To immortalize is to give enduring fame to someone or something.

The sculptor hoped to immortalize the fallen soldiers with a bronze statue that would stand in the town square for centuries.

Example

The band's biggest hit immortalized their hometown, drawing tourists to the small diner mentioned in the lyrics forty years later.

Immortalize means to preserve something in lasting fame -- through a monument, a work of art, or a story -- so it is remembered long after the moment has passed.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

commemorate: To commemorate is to honor the memory of a person or event -- a ceremony, a plaque, a moment of silence. It looks back with respect but does not create fame. To immortalize goes further: it fixes its subject in lasting public fame, so strangers know the name generations later.

enshrine: To enshrine is to set something apart as sacred or protected -- relics enshrined in a chapel, rights enshrined in a constitution. Immortalize is about fame rather than protection: an immortalized hero is widely remembered, not locked safely away.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

forget: fail to remember

erase: remove all trace of

Where it sits · how long the tribute lasts

remember → immortalize → deify

remember vs. immortalize: To remember is the mildest tribute and the most private -- you can remember a birthday with a card -- while to immortalize is to fix someone in public memory so firmly that strangers can name them generations on.

deify vs. immortalize: Deify goes a step beyond immortalize: an immortalized hero is remembered for centuries, while a deified one is worshipped as a god, the tribute renewed at every altar for as long as the faith survives.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-: not (Latin)

root — mortal: subject to death (Latin (mortalis))

suffix — -ize: to make or cause to become (Greek)

Put it together: im- ("not") + mortal ("subject to death") + -ize ("to make") = to make (someone or something) as if untouched by death -- to grant lasting fame.
